definitions.explanation: A pure and honest heart without any pretense or ulterior motives. Refers to genuine care, devotion, or goodwill.

examples.japanese: {真心|まごころ}を{込|こ}めて{作|つく}りました。
examples.english: I made it with all my heart.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}の{真心|まごころ}のこもったプレゼントに{感動|かんどう}した。
examples.english: I was moved by her heartfelt gift.

examples.japanese: お{客様|きゃくさま}に{真心|まごころ}を{込|こ}めたサービスを{提供|ていきょう}することが{私|わたし}たちの{使命|しめい}です。
examples.english: Our mission is to provide heartfelt service to our customers.

notes:
USAGE:
Most commonly appears in the phrase {真心|まごころ}を{込|こ}めて (with all one's heart, wholeheartedly). Frequently used in hospitality, gift-giving, and business contexts to express genuine care. It has a warm, somewhat elevated tone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {真心|まごころ}を{込|こ}めて: with all one's heart
- {真心|まごころ}のこもった: heartfelt, sincere
- {真心|まごころ}を{尽|つ}くす: to devote oneself sincerely

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {誠意|せいい}: sincerity, good faith (more formal, used in apologies and negotiations)
- {真摯|しんし}: earnest, sincere (na-adjective, emphasizes seriousness)
